title: What protects you, and what does not
h1: What protects you, and what does not
lede: An agent that acts for you is only acceptable if you can see what it did and stop it. Four mechanisms do that work: an identity you can rotate, an append-only audit log, recall, and permission red lines. Every item below names the file that implements it.
notice: This page describes mechanisms that exist in the current build. It is not a third-party audit, and no certification is claimed.

items.title: Your identity is a keypair, not an account
items.body: There is no central account that support can reset for you. That is the trade: nobody can take your identity away, and nobody can restore it either.

items.title: Moving devices rotates the key, it never copies it
items.body: Recovery is a proven key rotation. Your private key is not duplicated onto a new device, so a copy of an old device is not a copy of you.

items.title: The record lives on your device
items.body: Conversations, keys and logs are stored in a local database on your phone, and the app is built to keep working when no server is reachable.

items.title: Nothing is pulled automatically
items.body: Federation roster auto-pull ships off by default. Entries that arrive without your own pull are marked as auto-pulled, and can be cleared in one action.

items.title: Every action is written down
items.body: What your agent did on your behalf is recorded in an append-only log sealed with a Merkle root - later entries cannot silently rewrite earlier ones.

items.title: A message can be taken back
items.body: Recall withdraws a message after it went out. The log still records that it happened, so taking it back is not the same as erasing it.

items.title: Delegations can be revoked
items.body: Delegations and endorsements you issued can be revoked afterwards, and the revocation is itself recorded.

items.title: Calendar is read-only
items.body: The Android manifest declares READ_CALENDAR only - there is no WRITE_CALENDAR declaration anywhere in the app. Without the grant the feature degrades instead of failing.

proofNote: Each item names the file that implements it, and the verifier checks that the keyword is really present in that file.
boundary: Not a security audit. No third-party firm has reviewed this code, and no penetration test report exists.
Not a certification. No ISO, SOC 2 or equivalent claim is made anywhere on this site.
Not finished. Federation roster auto-pull is off by default, and the trial proxy is built but not yet connected to a live model provider.
